claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a homogeneous solid solution.
The as-synthesized catalyst is initially in a metallic state.
Potential cycling within the ethanol-oxidation potential window can selectively oxidize Ru sites.
The proposed potential cycling will minimally affect the other metal components.
Oxidizing Ru sites changes their local electronic structure.
Ru oxidation changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and its oxidative intermediates.
Ru oxidation alters the Ru d-band electronic structure.
The altered Ru d-band structure changes the binding energies of reactive intermediates.
Changes in intermediate binding strength affect intermediate conversion and therefore ethanol-oxidation behavior.
The Ru-oxidized catalyst will show a measurable difference in current density, product selectivity, or durability relative to the untreated catalyst.
If modified Ru sites contribute positively, pre-treatment may shift product distribution toward more favorable pathways.
The hypothesis is expected to apply in approximately 0.5 M sulfuric acid at 60–80 °C within a potential window that supports ethanol oxidation without extensive framework degradation.
Trends in similar alloy catalysts support an effect of Ru oxidation on local electronic properties.
A lack of statistically significant differences in activity, selectivity, and durability after selective Ru oxidation would falsify the proposed causal link.
